choices.title: Democratic leadership
choices.correct_explanation:
• Transactional leadership is the best answer to practice leadership. Transactional leaders identify what needs to be done to achieve goals, including clarifying roles and tasks, rewarding performance and providing for the social needs of followers.
  • The best leadership style is determined by the type of organization, working condition, type of employees, employer and outcome expected. There are various kinds of leadership style which are as follows:
  • Autocratic leadership style: Assumes that individuals are motivated by external forces, such as power, authority and need for approval; the leader makes all the decisions and uses coercion, punishment and direction to change followers’ and behaviors to achieve results.
  • Democratic leadership style: Assumes that individuals are motivated by internal drives and impulses, want active participation in decisions and want to get the task done; the leader uses participation and majority rule in setting goals and working towards achievement.
  • Bureaucratic leadership style: Assumes that employees are motivated by external forces. This leader trusts neither followers nor self to make decisions and therefore relies on organizational policies and rules to identify goals and direct work processes.
  • The laissez-faire leadership: Assumes that individuals are motivated by internal drives and impulses; they need to be left alone to make decisions about how to complete the work, the leader provides no direction or facilitation.
  • Charismatic leadership: It is based on personal qualities such as charm, persuasiveness personal power, self-confidence, extraordinary ideas and strong convictions. Few leaders possess genuine charisma.
  • Transformational leadership: Emphasizes the importance of interpersonal relationships. The goal is to generate employees’ commitment to the vision or ideal rather than to themselves

Reference:

  1. [Online] Available from https://online.stu.edu/articles/education/what-is-transactional-leadership.aspx. [Accessed June 2019]

choices.correct_explanation:
• Enterotoxigenic is the most common strain of E. coli giving rise to traveler diarrhea.
  • Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (E. coli) or ETEC, is an important cause of bacterial diarrheal illness. Infection with ETEC is the leading cause of travelers’ diarrhea and a major cause of diarrheal disease in lower-income countries, especially among children. ETEC is transmitted by food or water contaminated with animal or human feces. Infection can be prevented by avoiding or safely preparing foods and beverages that could be contaminated with the bacteria, as well as washing hands with soap frequently.
  • Enteropathogenic E. coli (or EPEC) is a special kind of E. coli that attaches itself to intestinal cells. It also causes diarrhea.
  • Enteroaggregative Escherichia coli (EAEC or EAggEC) are a pathotype of E. coli associated with acute and chronic diarrhea in both the developed and developing world. EAEC are defined by their “stacked-brick” pattern of adhesion to the human laryngeal epithelial cell line HEp-2.
  • Enteroinvasive Escherichia coli (EIEC) is a type of pathogenic bacteria whose infection causes a syndrome that is identical to shigellosis.

●       Licensure is granting the permission to carry out or practice in a profession after attaining a set of educational qualifications or passing a licensure entrance examination.

●       Registration is an important step to ensure that the nurse who has graduated from a nursing program met the requirements outlined by a country, state, province or similar licensing body can obtain a nursing license. An RN's scope of practice is determined by legislation and is regulated by a professional body or council. Licensure and registration are must to meet the nursing care.

●       Accreditation is a process whereby a professional association or nongovernmental agency grants recognition to a school or health care institution for demonstrated ability to meet predetermined criteria for established standards, such as the accreditation of hospitals by The Joint Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations (JACHO). Accreditation is most applicable for the hospitals or colleges, to ensure quality nursing education or meeting set standards of care in an institute.

●       Re-registration is a process of registering after a set period of time into the same organization for the same purpose. This happens in colleges before each semester.

Defense mechanisms may result in healthy or unhealthy consequences depending on the circumstances and frequency with which the mechanism is used. Examples of defense mechanism are regression, acting out, dissociation, compartmentalization, projection and reaction formation.
  • Psychosocial stage of development was given by Erickson, during each of Erikson’s eight development stages, two conflicting ideas must be resolved successfully for a person to become a confident, contributing member of society. Failure to master these tasks lead to feelings of inadequacy.
  • Psychosexual stage of development: Freud (1905) proposed that psychological development in childhood takes place in a series of fixed psychosexual stages: oral, anal, phallic, latency and genital.
  • In psychoanalytic theory, an excessive drive or demand may arise out of the strategies that individuals use to defend themselves against basic anxiety. Karen D. Horney enumerated 10 neurotic needs: for affection and approval, for a partner to take over one’s life, for restriction of one’s life, for power, for exploitation of others, for prestige, for admiration, for achievement, for self-sufficiency and independence and for perfection. When an individual’s personality is dominated by a few neurotic needs, he or she may exhibit a neurotic trend.

Reference:

choices.title: Early diagnosis and treatment
choices.correct_explanation:
Rationale (Secondary Prevention)
Secondary prevention is the level of prevention applied after the disease process has begun, usually in the early or asymptomatic stage, with the main aim of:

  • Early diagnosis
  • Prompt treatment
  • Screening for disease
  • Prevention of complications and disability

Therefore, the best answer is Early diagnosis and treatment.

Levels of Prevention 

1) Primordial prevention (Ideal)

  • Prevents: Risk factor development
  • Examples: Lifestyle modification, health education, sanitation, safe water

2) Primary prevention (Best)

  • Prevents: Disease occurrence
  • Examples: Specific protection, immunization, pre-employment checkup, pre-exposure prophylaxis, presumptive screening, chemoprophylaxis, food fortification

3) Secondary prevention (Most common)

  • Prevents: Complications and disability
  • Includes: Early diagnosis, prompt treatment, screening for disease, disability (complication) prevention

4) Tertiary prevention

  • Prevents: Disability and death
  • Examples: Disability limitation, rehabilitation, prosthesis, transplants

Distractor Rationales

Option B: Rehabilitation and disability limitation — Incorrect

This is tertiary prevention, not secondary.

Option C: Specific protection and screening — Incorrect

This is a mixed option:

  • Specific protection = primary prevention
  • Screening = secondary prevention

Option D: Screening and immunization — Incorrect

This is also a mixed option:

  • Screening = secondary prevention
  • Immunization = primary prevention
